checklist.notes: The personal-information examples and present-simple target are suitable for A1.1, but the unsupported learner-facing directions repeatedly rely on language well beyond A1.1, including ‘signals a routine’, ‘stable’, ‘ridge’, ‘continues briefly’, and the conditional troubleshooting sequence.

The present-simple meaning contrast and the I/you/we/they versus he/she forms are accurate. The /v/, /z/, and syllable-count descriptions are materially accurate as introductory pronunciation guidance.
The personal model and core English examples are natural. One compressed articulatory instruction is recorded as a minor finding but does not make the lesson globally unnatural.

Internal comparison found no suspicious unexplained copying; only expected overlap in target forms and project-authored concepts was observed. External originality was not tested and is explicitly limited.
The lesson introduces only present simple and phoneme work, uses the authorized skill/topic concepts, and assumes no unlisted curriculum prerequisite.
All learner-facing material is English, and every embedded concept or vocabulary reference is within the regenerated authoritative request scope.

methods: Manual comparison of lesson wording with the supplied authoritative request and project-authored teaching payload.
Exact contiguous-word overlap comparison across the ten supplied v3 lesson bodies.
Inspection of the accepted audit provenance/copyright scope without consulting external sources.
copyright_originality_check.scope_limitations: No suspicious unexplained copying was found within the supplied scope. Reuse of target forms, short pedagogical frames, and project-authored definitions/examples is expected. No external search was performed; this is not a plagiarism clearance or copyright guarantee.

findings.description: Sections 1, 3, and 4 require an A1.1 learner to process dense unsupported metalinguistic and articulatory prose (‘signals’, ‘stable’, ‘ridge’, ‘continues briefly’, ‘rebuild sound → word → sentence’). This learner-facing language can prevent comprehension of the core task even though the example sentences themselves are level-appropriate.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite directions as short high-frequency steps, demonstrate each physical action concretely, and add controlled Vietnamese or visual scaffolding where needed.

findings.description: ‘Lip plus teeth signals /v/’ is compressed, non-idiomatic instructional wording.
findings.recommendation: Use a direct instruction such as ‘Touch your lower lip with your upper teeth for /v/.’

limitations: Review used only the exact lesson, accepted audit, regenerated hash-matching authoritative request, and verified M5 development snapshot; generator reasoning and prior review records were excluded.
No audio was supplied; pronunciation judgments cover written instructions and IPA only, not realized speech or learner performance.
No external CEFR vocabulary profiler or corpus was used; CEFR findings are qualitative independent AI judgments about the learner-facing text.

Originality checking was limited to the supplied authoritative payload and the ten supplied v3 lessons; no Internet, external corpus, or plagiarism search was performed, so no external plagiarism or legal-clearance claim is made.
